text: CROSS-FIRMWARE (CM550 selectSensorRawChannels @ 0x1d392 vs CM848 cm848_selectHighSpeedGovernorGainSet @ 0x1fa20): SAME FUNCTION, relocation-map status 'similar' (one real code difference, below). Same algorithm and constants line by line: when the feature word bit 0 is set (CM550 _feature_enable_flags_word, CM848 system_feature_config_flags) a pass counter x 20 (0x14) is the transient timer; while the second-stage filtered engine acceleration is above a threshold (CM550 hsg_acceleration_rate_threshold_for_transient_conditions @0x808118 = CM848 DAT_0005c314) and the previous mode word is not 12 (CM550 DAT_0080d33c, CM848 governor_mode_code_prev) the transient set (code 17) is loaded once and the counter restarts at 0; once the transient time (CM550 hsg_acceleration_reference_time_for_transient_conditions @0x80811a = DAT_0005c316) has passed, the low / high reference-speed set (codes 18 / 19; thresholds CM550 hsg_speed_threshold_for_low_reference_speed_region @0x808126 = DAT_0005c322 and ..._high_... @0x80811c = DAT_0005c318) or the base set (code 16) is written to the alternate set and, when the working-set code is 0, to the live set (else the working set is copied and its code kept); the error filter coefficient pointer is aimed at the live coefficient (CM550 _DAT_0080d636). CM550 CODE <-> CM848 DATA: every ROM word the CM848 function reads (DAT_0005c314-0x5c332, 16 words, all lhz) sits at the same relative offset as the CM550 constants it reads (0x808118-0x808136); the seven CM550 words that carry e2m names (0x808118, 0x80811a, 0x80811c, 0x808120, 0x808126, 0x80812a, 0x808132) all coincide with the CM848 words used for the same purpose (0x5c314, 0x5c316, 0x5c318, 0x5c31c, 0x5c322, 0x5c326, 0x5c32e). THE ONE DIFFERENCE: CM848 has an else branch for 'feature bit 0 clear' that copies the base gains / error filter coefficient into the live set and sets code 16 on every pass; CM550 does nothing in that case (the live set keeps its start value). Naming side note: CM550 calls the LIVE selected set hsg_proportional_gain_base / hsg_integral_gain_base / hsg_derivative_gain_base (its calibrated base set is DAT_00808036-0x80803c) while CM848 calls the live set high_speed_governor_*_gain and the calibrated set *_base. PROPOSAL (one unprefixed name for both; it is free in both function_renames.csv; both files only have the old names): CM550 function_renames.csv row (two columns, replaces line 371): 0x0001d392,selectHighSpeedGovernorGainSet | CM848 function_renames.csv row (replaces line 843; unprefixed because the function is now shared): 0x0001fa20,selectHighSpeedGovernorGainSet,Selects the high speed governor gain set - error filter coefficient plus proportional, integral and derivative gains - and records its code in high_speed_governor_gain_set_code: the base set (code 16) when system_feature_config_flags bit 0 is clear; otherwise a transient set (code 17, DAT_0005c32c-0x5c332) while engine acceleration is above DAT_0005c314 and governor_mode_code_prev is not 12, and once the transient time DAT_0005c316 has elapsed the working set (when loaded) or the low / high reference speed set (codes 18 / 19, chosen by engine_speed_limit_arbitrated against DAT_0005c322 / DAT_0005c318; base set 16 between them); it also records the alternate set (was selectSensorRawChannels then cm848_selectHighSpeedGovernorGainSet; CM550 0x1d392 is the same function).

CROSS-FIRMWARE side finding (first look, not verified further): CM550 cm550_FUN_0001d5a0 (the next function) is the counterpart of CM848 cm848_selectEngineSpeedLimit: a lowest-wins arbitration of the HSG reference speed that records the winner in hsg_reference_speed_winning_source_indicator (values 8 / 5 / 6 / 9 / 4 / 3 / 2); its value 9 is the datalink speed-control-mode-3 speed limit, which matches CM848 limiting_source_number 9 (TSC1 governor mode 3 limit). If the owner agrees, the same unprefixed-name treatment applies.
